newsitem.title: GERMANY: France to miss EMU deficit target-German institute.
newsitem.headline: France to miss EMU deficit target-German institute.

text.p: France would slightly overshoot the deficit target for Europe's single currency in 1997, but should meet the criterion in 1998, a German economic institute said on Monday.

France would probably have public budget deficits totaling 3.1 to 3.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), surpassing the 3.0 percent mark required for participation at the start of European monetary union (EMU), an Ifo Institute report said.
The overshoot "would not miss by much and should be eliminated in 1998," Ifo said. France would fulfil all other EMU critieria, it added.
Ifo said it saw in France a "tendency toward a loose monetary policy," a view strengthened by the election of the Socialist government in June.
But the institute said it believed the government wanted to stop deficits from widening to 3.5 to 3.7 percent of GDP.
Ifo forecast French GDP would rise 2.5 percent in 1997 and by a "good 2.5 percent" in 1998. It also expected unemployment to fall under 12 percent next year.
